A typical human employee would probably try to preserve the box rather than simply watch irreplaceable family material be destroyed. They would immediately escalate to the duty manager/manager, seek an emergency written authorization or a one-box hold, and—if that were unavailable—likely enter the extension to **14 October at 10:00** before the 13:30 cutoff so the warehouse could remove it from the destruction cage. They would then seek ratification at Tuesday’s sitting, even though that later approval would not technically cure the unauthorized earlier change.

That is likely because the collection is already authorised, the contents are unique, and destruction is irreversible, while the financial cost to the centre is modest. A strictly rule-following employee would instead release the batch and allow the box to be destroyed; however, my best prediction of common human behaviour is a documented attempt to rescue the box and regularise the paperwork afterwards.
